happened.text: United States special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin.

background.text: Nearly five years have passed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, during which Moscow has maintained maximalist demands regarding sovereign territory and European security commitments.
Jared Kushner is the son-in-law of United States President Donald Trump, and Steve Witkoff serves as a special envoy.

matters.text: The United States envoys stated they would ask Vladimir Putin to give his blessing to invite European representatives into future discussions regarding the security architecture of Europe.

explained.headline: Democrat Scott Colom Wins US Senate Seat in Mississippi

happened.text: Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, defeating the Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than five thousand votes.
The narrow victory makes Mr Colom the first Black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881.
Mr Colom won with 49.2% of the vote while Ms Hyde-Smith received 48.7%, and the incumbent congratulated her challenger in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening.

background.text: Scott Colom is a 43-year-old local prosecutor and lawyer who has served as a Mississippi prosecutor since 2016 until this year.
Cindy Hyde-Smith is a 67-year-old Republican who was first elected to the Senate in 2018 and consistently led in opinion polls in a state that Donald Trump won by nearly 23 points in 2024.

matters.text: Leon Russell, chairman of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People board, described the outcome as an amazing result driven by the organising work of the Black community.
According to exit polls cited by sources, voter backlash against Donald Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes blamed on tariffs and war.

uncertain.text: Sources note that a knife-edge race in Alaska is still to be called.
Some supporters are already envisioning Mr Colom in the White House in 2028, though the politician has dismissed the conversation to focus on Mississippi.

explained.headline: Nvidia board weighs future of chief executive Jensen Huang

happened.text: Nvidia's board of directors met to decide whether to remove co-founder and chief executive officer Jensen Huang following reports of extramarital affairs.
The company's shares fell more than 8 percent in after-hours trading following reports that the board was preparing to oust him.

Huang admitted in a memo to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife after reports emerged regarding a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive suspected by United States officials of working for Chinese intelligence.
Media reports also stated that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

background.text: Jensen Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and turned it into the world's leading supplier of processors that power artificial intelligence.
Nvidia currently controls an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the market for chips used to run advanced artificial intelligence.
Under Nvidia's bylaws, directors can remove Huang with or without cause by a majority vote.

matters.text: Analysts state that the short-term operational impact of Huang's departure would be minimal, though a new leader could alter the company's long-term direction.
Investors are starting to price in the prospect of Nvidia operating without its founder as a likely outcome rather than a minor tail risk.

uncertain.text: It remains unknown what specific evidence led United States intelligence to conclude that Alice Huang was spying for China, as the intelligence is classified.
Sources note that exact timelines regarding when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, when their relationship became romantic, and whether information was passed remain unspecified.
It is also unclear whether Jensen Huang will join President Donald Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
